title: Melian Starguard
type: Pristinian civic leader; keeper of continuity
dek: A civic leader who remains responsible for Pristinia through miracles, wars, betrayals, deaths, returns and the departure of its adventurers.

body:
Melian Starguard remains responsible for Pristinia as adventurers arrive, fight gods, betray one another, die, return and move on. Many have greater wealth, magic, mobility or destructive power than she does; she still has to help run the town after their interventions.

Pristinia still needs food, labor, walls, diplomacy, funerals, public property and trust after an adventurer’s intervention ends. The strength to win a fight does not itself confer authority over those civic affairs.

Interpreter of a vulnerable settlement

In Pristinia’s earliest recovered history, Melian meets newcomers over a map and leads them through the settlement whose needs will shape their work. By August 2024 she can explain the town’s geopolitical position among Rahu influence, Eovar, the Guardians of the Shard, and The Before. Her leadership predates the siege: she knows the region, interprets it for outsiders, and carries institutional memory.

The last banner of Pristinia

During the Rahu crisis, Ada’s frightened chronicle calls Melian the last banner of Pristinia. She takes position at the Northeast Tower and helps organize the town’s defense, using its palisades and terrain and the work of smiths, miners, crafters, and loyalists. Elenia’s later extraordinary intervention can break siege engines; Melian remains responsible for the town before, during, and after that intervention.

4 June 2025 · political abduction

Melian is alone with tea when Magnus and the Rahu arrive. She rises, draws her sword, and faces a consequence she has anticipated without pretending she can guarantee victory.

I knew this day would come. Let us see what comes of it.Melian Starguard

Magnus immediately uses yielding gas. Melian collapses, is wrapped to resemble a corpse, and is carried away. The Rahu target her not because she is Pristinia’s most dangerous combatant, but because she represents it institutionally. The attack is political kidnapping rather than an ordinary battlefield defeat.

Herb and Scout Lilian approach while Herb carries a meal meant to cheer her. Magnus orders both witnesses killed. The operation therefore wounds Melian’s office, body, friendships, and civilian community at the same time.

Leadership as remaining

Melian survives into Pristinia’s later history, although the details of her captivity and return remain incomplete. She witnesses the Rahu crisis, the growth of adventurer factions, the destruction and rebuilding of institutions, and Papirak’s death. Her later public work continues the history interrupted by her kidnapping.

Papirak’s funeral · carrying the flame

On 30 September 2026, Melian leads the procession and performs the Rite of the Flame. Her language makes survival an obligation to carry something forward for those who cannot.

What light they leave behind...... now lives within my hands.Melian Starguard
I walk because they cannot, and I shine... where they are gone.Melian Starguard

Papirak’s walking stick is revealed as a Staff of Power worth an enormous sum. Melian refuses to reduce its meaning to utility and determines that it belongs with Papirak. When Fenwick Sequesters it with Pell’s permission and Camilla can no longer detect it, Melian trusts them enough to continue the rite. Suspicion remains part of the history; it does not become proof of theft.

The flame and the hearth

At the funeral, Melian leads the rite and gives the town words for its loss. Herb brings people together afterward through food, drink and laughter. Their friendship also appears in an earlier, quieter act: he carries dinner through a war zone because he knows she is struggling. No formal declaration supplies the full history of that bond.

The open record

Melian’s exact title and constitutional powers at each stage, early biography, founding role, complete captivity and return, pre-war friendship with Herb, and authority over Pristinia’s council, treasury, militia, and adventurers remain unresolved. “Major civic leader” is established; a more specific office must wait for evidence.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes preserve what was knowable when people acted. Dates below identify source postings in UTC; they do not supply an in-world calendar. A later appearance does not settle present status.

  1. 2024-03-12 · quest

    A town’s name meets its actual size

    Melian favors Pristinia while questioning John’s grander wording for a small settlement.

    Known at this stage
    The name is being discussed, rather than remembered as an inevitable foundation myth.
    Consequence
    Her practical civic voice is visible early.
    Still unresolved
    The exchange does not establish a sole founder or erase the other participants.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

  2. 2025-06-05 · quest

    Absence is discovered before its explanation

    Narration places Herb, Lillian and the raven dead near Melian’s open house, with Melian missing.

    Known at this stage
    At discovery, her location and the attackers’ full story are still unknown.
    Consequence
    The crisis begins as a search and an investigation.
    Still unresolved
    The narrator places the event on the preceding day; the receipt’s posting date is not the abduction date.

    Receipt 1

Peace and a reported release

The first investigation is posted on 5 June 2025, but its narrator explicitly places it on the preceding day, soon after the deaths were discovered. A later search scene must not turn that posting boundary into another day of events.

At the close of the peace negotiations, Olokun insists that the delegation leave with Melian. Ephraith answers that the war is over and Melian has already been released. The statement supplies a missing link between captivity and her later public life, while remaining the Queen’s report. The handover, route home, conditions of confinement and exact release time are not witnessed in this passage.

relationshipMap.title: Melian Starguard’s relationship web
relationshipMap.intro: Melian’s authority is measured by what remains after extraordinary people leave: a town, its procedures, its dead, and the responsibility to keep deciding. Select a tie to follow that civic burden through crisis and remembrance.

nodes.title: Herb Shepard
nodes.subtitle: The hearth beside the flame
nodes.history: Herb brings Melian a special meal during the Rahu crisis and is killed during her abduction. Both later return to Pristinia’s life, where Melian carries formal remembrance and Herb gathers the living afterward.
nodes.consequence: Their paired history joins civic leadership to hospitality. The flame and the hearth are different forms of keeping a community alive.
nodes.evidence: The meal, murder, later presence, and funeral roles are established; the mechanics between death and return remain incomplete.

nodes.title: Magnus Niriin
nodes.subtitle: The returning adventurer who abducts her
nodes.relation: Civic authority targeted by covert force
nodes.history: Magnus returns as leader of a Rahu operation, incapacitates Melian with yielding gas, disguises her as a corpse, orders the killing of witnesses, and delivers her to Strange Talon.
nodes.consequence: The abduction demonstrates how quickly adventurer power can become violence against the settlement it once moved through. Melian’s later survival does not cancel the political rupture.
nodes.evidence: The operation is directly preserved; captivity, release, and full aftermath remain unresolved.

nodes.title: Elenia
nodes.subtitle: Intervention beside continuity
nodes.history: During Pristinia’s crisis, Melian organizes civic resistance while Elenia embodies the extraordinary intervention capable of changing a battlefield.
nodes.consequence: The contrast prevents either role from consuming the other. A town needs someone able to act against catastrophe and someone responsible for what still exists when the intervention ends.
nodes.evidence: Their distinct crisis functions are established; a complete personal relationship chronology is not.

nodes.title: Papirak
nodes.subtitle: A light carried after death
nodes.relation: Public memory made into civic stewardship
nodes.history: Melian leads Papirak’s Rite of the Flame and argues that his Staff of Power should remain his final worldly possession rather than become a liquid asset or prize.
nodes.consequence: Her decision treats power, property, and grief as questions the community must answer without converting the dead into resources for the living.
nodes.evidence: The rite, public discussion, and burial decision are directly preserved.

nodes.title: Camilla Blackwood
nodes.subtitle: Security suspicion at the tomb
nodes.history: After Fenwick casts Sequester on Papirak’s staff, Camilla can no longer detect it and warns Melian that it may have been stolen. Melian trusts Pell and Fenwick and continues the funeral.
nodes.consequence: The disagreement preserves a real civic tension: security vigilance can be sincere without making its interpretation fact, while trust remains a decision made under uncertainty.
nodes.evidence: Camilla’s observation, interpretation, and Melian’s response are established; theft is not.

nodes.title: Pristinia
nodes.subtitle: The constituency that remains
nodes.history: Melian briefs newcomers, organizes resistance, survives being made a political hostage, and later conducts public remembrance while adventurers and divine powers move through the settlement.
nodes.consequence: Her record asks what legitimate civic authority looks like when residents depend on people whose power exceeds local institutions and whose presence is temporary.
nodes.evidence: These public roles are established; her exact constitutional title and powers remain unresolved.

insights.label: Central constituency
insights.note: Leadership is answerable to the people who remain after heroes leave.

insights.note: The flame and hearth preserve different parts of communal life.
